newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Agriculture to reduce Brazil's trade deficit-paper.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture to reduce Brazil's trade deficit-paper.

text.p: Brazil's agricultural exports are forecast to increase by $1.3 billion in 1997, representing its most important weapon in the battle against a burgeoning trade deficit, the daily newspaper Folha de Sao Paulo said.
Soybeans and soy products alone are seen contributing an extra $500 million in export revenues this year, the paper said.
The main factors behind the increase are a bumper harvest and the abolition of the ICMS export tax on raw and semi-manufactured goods in September 1996.
Agricultural export revenues jumped to $14.51 billion in 1996 from $9.29 billion in 1992, representing 30.82 percent of total exports last year, Folha said.
Brazil reported a trade deficit of $5.5 billion in 1996. This was set to increase to $12 billion in 1997, according to Folha.
The country plans to move from exporting specialty products like tropical fruits and flowers to a second phase of exporting consumer electronics and computer technology, the paper added.
